card.title: THE BLEEDERS
card.text: Gets +1+1 when you play a card with Bond.
card.flavorText: The Somerset Light Infantry, nicknamed “The Bleeders,” traced its origins to 1685, having been raised in response to the Monmouth Rebellion. By the outbreak of WWII, the regiment had already fought in numerous major conflicts. During the early years of the war, its battalions served across India, Burma, and the Middle East. The 1st Battalion saw extensive combat in the Burma Campaign, enduring some of the most punishing conditions of the war. Deployed in 1942 to counter the Japanese advance into India, it later participated in the critical battles of Kohima and Imphal, helping to halt the Japanese offensive. The regiment’s light infantry training made it particularly well-suited for the region's mountainous terrain and dense jungles. Meanwhile, the 7th Battalion served with distinction in North Africa and Italy. The 10th Battalion, originally a hostilities-only unit, was converted into the 7th Parachute Battalion in 1943. It went on to fight in Normandy, the Ardennes, and across the Rhine during the final Allied push into Germany. Finally, the 30th Battalion, part of the 43rd Infantry Brigade under the British First Army, saw active service in both Tunisia and Italy.
